newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel- HS barges fall on Mideast, cargoes hold.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel- HS barges fall on Mideast, cargoes hold.

text.p: High sulphur cracked barges dropped sharply on Monday as easing tension in the Middle East stripped away the main bullish factor.

High sulphur cargoes and other fuel oil grades were steady or slightly firmer, indicating the market has some fundamental strength on the back of tight supplies. Activity was very slow as the market digested recent events which have knocked 70 cents off Brent futures.
High sulphur barges traded at $110 fob ARA in a lacklustre market, off $7-8 from Friday. High sulphur cargoes were softer by about $1 at $107-108 fob NWE.
Some dealers thought there might be further pressure on prices since end-user demand for September was not seen even though supplies were tightish.
The low sulphur cracked barge market was very illiquid with offers at $117 fob ARA, but buyers not showing any interest.

Physical prompt cargoes were steady around $116-118 fob NWE. "Wet barrels lagged behind last week, so there has been little room to fall," said one dealer. A trader was heard bidding in the high $120s cif Med into Turkey although several dealers thought product sourced from the U.S. contango into October remains. -- Matthew Jones, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 8980
